New LLM beats benchmarks in machine learning test

By A. Writer

A research lab released a new large language model on Monday that it says outperforms previous systems on a wide range of reasoning and coding benchmarks. The company described the model as a significant step forward for machine learning systems used in everyday software.

Independent researchers cautioned that benchmark results do not always translate into better performance on real tasks, and that careful evaluation by third parties will take several weeks. Several groups have already begun running their own tests on the model's public interface.

What changed

According to the technical report, the improvements come mostly from better training data and a longer training schedule rather than a new architecture. The lab also said it spent more effort on safety testing than for any previous release, including red-teaming by outside experts.

  • Better reasoning scores
  • Faster responses
  • Lower prices for developers

Pricing for developers will be lower than the previous generation, the company said, and the model will be available through the usual cloud platforms starting next week. Enterprise customers will receive access first, followed by a broader rollout to individual developers.

We think this is the most useful model we have built so far, the lab's director said.

Analysts expect competitors to respond with their own releases before the end of the year, as the race to build more capable systems continues to accelerate across the industry.
